concept: Atlas Infinite oplog and storage cost
summary: Source-anchored research for Atlas Infinite oplog and storage cost. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The local.oplog.rs collection counts toward stored data and storage charges on Atlas Infinite even though storage-layer replication replaces its traditional replication role. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas does not bill data replicated internally within the Infinite storage layer as data transfer. That exemption does not make the retained oplog collection free storage. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
Operators can read local.oplog.rs with read privileges on the local database, but cannot configure an oplog byte size on Atlas Infinite. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas Infinite meters primary storage hourly in uncompressed logical GB-hours, independently of compute; logical data size includes uncompressed collections and indexes rather than provisioned physical disk capacity. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

On Atlas Infinite, local.oplog.rs supports change streams and limited-history internal functions rather than node replication. Its retention window limits how far an interrupted change stream can resume. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Cost-model inference: sustained write churn or a longer minimum oplog retention window can increase billable logical storage even if the live application dataset stays approximately constant. Estimate retained oplog separately from live data; validate with measured usage rather than treating retention hours as a fixed byte allocation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The architecture documentation gives a default minimum oplog retention window of 24 hours and allows changes in Additional Settings; entries older than the configured window are deleted. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Compute nodes share managed storage. Resizing compute does not itself change storage billing, so pricing storage as a separate full logical database copy for each compute node would misrepresent the documented billing model. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The engineering design uses a logical oplog for Log Service durability and a separate physical phylog for checkpoint page materialization. This internal logging description must be distinguished from operational guidance about local.oplog.rs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-08)

Increasing the Atlas Infinite compute tier can improve throughput and IOPS without changing its storage-capacity ceiling; independent storage capacity therefore does not imply unlimited throughput at a small compute tier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Budgeting inference: with the same write workload and unchanged application data, retaining more oplog history can increase billable logical GB-hours even if the compute tier stays fixed; neither cited page supplies a universal dollar amount for that increase. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The Weighted Average recommends recording logical data separately from allocated storage and validating the supplier estimate against a trial invoice. This is independent evaluation advice, not a measured result establishing oplog savings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-30)

Talking Tech cautions that preview performance and availability numbers are MongoDB's own, while TechTarget explicitly attributes the reported Infinite throughput tests to MongoDB. Neither source supplies an independent oplog billing measurement. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
